speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Can you describe the bleeding from your wisdom tooth extraction in detail, and have you experienced easy bruising elsewhere on your body?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient was brought in by his mother for persistent bleeding following elective removal of wisdom teeth. The bleeding from the surrounding gums was minimally responsive to multiple gauze packs. The patient also has a history of easy bruising. Family history includes the patient's uncle who had similar issues with bleeding and a history of easy bruising and joint swelling.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Do you have a personal history of joint swelling or bleeding into joints, and does your family history suggest an X-linked pattern with affected males?
REQUEST TEST: Coagulation Profile, Factor VIII and Factor IX Levels

speaker: Doctor
text:
Since coagulation factors are normal, I need to check for a platelet function defect. Do you experience frequent nosebleeds or bleeding from your gums when brushing?
REQUEST TEST: Bleeding Time, Platelet Function Assay

speaker: Doctor
text:
Given the normal coagulation profile but prolonged bleeding time and family history, I suspect a platelet adhesion defect like von Willebrand Disease. Do you have a history of frequent nosebleeds or heavy menstrual bleeding if applicable, and have you ever had bleeding after other minor surgeries or dental work?
REQUEST TEST: von Willebrand Factor Antigen, von Willebrand Factor Activity

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: von Willebrand Factor Antigen: Low, von Willebrand Factor Activity: Low

speaker: Doctor
text: The low von Willebrand factor antigen and activity levels confirm the diagnosis of von Willebrand Disease. DIAGNOSIS READY: von Willebrand Disease
